related_questions.question: Can you improve your sense of smell?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, it is possible to improve your sense of smell, especially if it has been temporarily reduced due to illness or other factors. Smell training, a process of regularly sniffing specific scents, can help reawaken olfactory nerves and reconnect them with the brain's smell processing center.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, it is possible to improve your sense of smell, especially if it has been temporarily reduced due to illness or other factors

text_blocks.snippet: Here's how you can improve your sense of smell:

list.title: Choose scents:
list.snippet: Select at least four distinct scents, such as lemon (citrus), rose (floral), cloves (spicy), and eucalyptus (resinous), according to ENT Health.

list.title: Smell regularly:
list.snippet: Sniff each scent for 10-20 seconds, twice a day, for several months, focusing on the memory and sensation of the smell.

list.title: Be patient:
list.snippet: It may take time for the olfactory nerves to recover and for smells to return, so don't get discouraged.

list.title: Associate smells with memories:
list.snippet: Connecting smells to positive memories can help strengthen the association and improve recall.

list.title: Eat foods rich in zinc and vitamin B12:
list.snippet: These nutrients are important for overall health, including the sense of smell, says a doctor from losangelesentdoctor.com.

list.title: Treat underlying conditions:
list.snippet: If your sense of smell is affected by a sinus infection, nasal polyps, or other conditions, seek treatment from a doctor.

list.title: Clean your nasal passages:
list.snippet: Rinsing with a saline solution can help clear congestion and improve airflow.
If you are experiencing significant or persistent loss of smell, consult with an ENT (Ear, Nose, and Throat) specialist.
They can assess your condition and recommend appropriate treatment options, including smell retraining therapy or other therapies.
